summary: L001 passed the fixed G01 positive-Tc guard (8.5582 K <= 8.8322 K) but did not improve the A05 incumbent: pooled weighted OOF MAE was 7.7935 K versus 7.7526 K, a deterioration of 0.0409 K. Relative to A05, positive-Tc MAE also worsened from 8.5051 K to 8.5582 K, reported-zero MAE worsened from 6.0806 K to 6.0945 K, and high-Tc MAE worsened from 28.8502 K to 29.0608 K. Thus, changing only the omitted fe_anion fallback from extra_trees/raw to hist_gradient_boosting/raw was guard-eligible but uniformly unfavorable on the reported metrics.
next_focus: Use the final experiment to test the remaining focused fe_anion alternative around A05: composition input, chemistry routing, global extra_trees/raw, extra_trees/raw experts for cu_o and other, and a hist_gradient_boosting/raw expert for fe_anion. A01 showed that a route-specific extra_trees/raw fe_anion expert was worse than A05's broad extra_trees/raw fallback, while L001 showed that a broad hist_gradient_boosting/raw fallback was also worse; this untried configuration isolates whether hist_gradient_boosting becomes useful only when specialized to fe_anion. It is falsified as an eligible improvement if pooled OOF MAE is not below 7.752598770753422 K or positive-Tc MAE exceeds 8.832165507919859 K.
limitations: All results are adaptive development evidence from the same fixed-group training OOF folds, not independent validation.
The chemistry routes are operational composition partitions rather than verified physical families.
The fe_anion route is relatively small (285 rows, 37 groups), so its expert estimate may be unstable.
Large cu_o errors remain, including severe overprediction of some reported-zero materials and underprediction of high-Tc materials.
